description: Foundation (pure, no egui behaviour change yet): add the persisted optional `description` field to the alias row model and working-copy row, and build the shared ISPF table-editor component's PURE core -- the IspfTableHost trait + column model, the ff-line-commands-backed line-command apply pass over a generic Vec<Row>, and the stable Sort -- all unit-tested without egui. Also factor the single `alias_sort_key` helper (uppercased surface asc, canonical tie-break) that both the manual SORT and the auto-sort-on-save will share. This leaves the Alias editor rendering exactly as today (it does not yet consume the shared render); it only adds the field and the new pure modules, so the crate stays buildable. Resolver (AliasTable::canonical_verb) is UNTOUCHED.
steps: READ FIRST: context.json, this file, docs/specs/ispf-table-editor/{requirements,design}.md, docs/specs/command-configurator/requirements.md Req 7, and the files crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/user_aliases.rs, alias_editor_panel/state.rs, shell/alias_editor.rs, shell/alias_reader.rs, and crates/ff-line-commands/src/{lib,command,parser}.rs.

Add `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty")] pub description: String` to UserAliasRowToml (crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/user_aliases.rs), after command_template. TDD: first extend the in-file round-trip tests to assert (a) a row with a description round-trips through serialise/parse, and (b) an old file with NO description key loads with description == "" and re-serialises WITHOUT emitting an empty description. Confirm they fail, then implement.

In crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/alias_reader.rs: read effective_display_rows() and the shipped-seed AliasRowToml and apply_user_overlay_from_base. Extend the effective-row shape (and AliasRowToml if it carries the field) so a saved description reloads (Req 7.3 round-trip). If extending the tuple is heavy, add description as an additional element and update the single caller load_effective_alias_rows. Keep ASCII-only. Add/extend a test proving seed+override preserves description.

Thread description through crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/alias_editor.rs: validate_user_alias_rows carries row.description.trim() into the emitted UserAliasRowToml; load_effective_alias_rows populates AliasRowEdit.description from the effective row. Do NOT change the validation rules otherwise.

Create the shared module crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/ispf_table_editor/ with mod.rs (re-exports) + state.rs: the generic IspfTableHost trait (columns() -> &[ColumnSpec], line_command_set() -> LineCommandSet, blank_row()/clone_row()/filter_matches()/sort helpers), ColumnSpec { id, header, filterable, compare_mode, sortable }, LineCommandSet (enabled letters), FilterState, and a TableEditorState (command_line + filter). Register `mod ispf_table_editor;` in crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/mod.rs (alphabetical). TDD: unit tests that a ColumnSpec round-trips its filterable/sortable flags and compare mode, and a LineCommandSet reports its enabled letters.

Implement crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/ispf_table_editor/line_commands.rs: the PURE apply pass over a generic Vec<Row> via the host, sourcing classification from ff_line_commands (LineCommandParser::parse + command::classify). I inserts host.blank_row() after; D removes; immediate commands processed by DESCENDING index; C + A/B pairing via the engine's Source/Target categories (an unresolved C source RETAINED with a non-blocking notice, not discarded); R (if enabled) = clone-after; unrecognised/not-enabled letters cleared and ignored. Return a small result carrying any notice. TDD FIRST with a stub Row + stub host: I-after, D-remove, mixed I/D descending-index integrity, C+A copy-after, C+B copy-before, unresolved-C retained, unrecognised cleared.

Implement the Sort core in crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/ispf_table_editor/sort.rs (re-exported from mod.rs): a STABLE sort over the backing Vec<Row> by a host-declared key column, ASC default, `SORT <column> [ASC|DESC]` arg parsing, and a no-sortable-column no-op that returns a non-blocking notice. TDD FIRST: stable ASC/DESC, no-op on no sortable column, reorders the backing list.

Factor `alias_sort_key(surface: &str, canonical: &str) -> (String, String)` (uppercased surface, uppercased canonical tie-break) into ONE place (crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/user_aliases.rs or the shared sort module) so FEAT-002's manual SORT and auto-sort-on-save use it identically. Unit-test the key ordering.
Keep every new/changed .rs file under 400 NON-TEST lines; if shell/alias_editor.rs approaches the limit, split its #[cfg(test)] mod into a sibling file rather than growing it. ASCII-only.
acceptance_criteria: UserAliasRowToml and AliasRowEdit both carry a description field; a description round-trips through serialise/parse and an older file without the field still loads (default empty) and re-serialises without an empty description key.
A saved description reloads through the effective-row load path (seed + override) -- proven by a test.
crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/ispf_table_editor/{mod,state,line_commands,sort}.rs exist and compile; the apply pass and sort are pure (no egui) and fully unit-tested per the steps.
The line-command apply pass reuses ff-line-commands for classification (no new parser) and keeps index integrity on a mixed I/D batch; C+A/B pairing works and an unresolved C is retained.
A single alias_sort_key helper exists and is unit-tested (uppercased surface asc, canonical tie-break).
The alias resolver (shell/environment.rs AliasTable::canonical_verb) is unchanged; no ff-line-commands public API change.
Every touched/new .rs file is <=400 non-test lines; all content ASCII-only.
